name: @olai/tests
//scripts: Bun hosts the runner, and `test` NAMES cucumber's entry file so that it does — never the `cucumber-js` bin, whose `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang is resolved against PATH and hands the suite to whatever node the host has. README.md tells that story; runner.test.ts pins the spelling. Keep it a path: this one is stable because the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) gives every package its own direct dependencies.
//dependencies: The e2e runner imports static contracts for the workflows it drives. @olai/web supplies its curated testlib (attributes, deadlines, theme and dates); @olai/bundle supplies the combined testids; @olai/fonts and @olai/appearance supply display policy; @olai/ui-primitives supplies shared UI names. @olai/format supplies MARKS and literal test claims, and @olai/surface supplies mediaHref and sealPolicy. The suite's own support/world.ts composes ROW_TESTID from the testids doors of outlines, markdown, hypertext, csv, image and pdf — the five body-row dependencies are names only, not plugin activations. Files supplies minting names, layout supplies its persisted width, outlines supplies record UI contracts, and chat and alerts supply their UI names. Identity supplies proxy-header and avatar contracts. Kolu supplies its fake appliance testlib. @olai/plugin-api supplies the host contracts used by test plugins, and @olai/log supplies the test log collector. These are explicit dependencies of the driver; the bundle's import fences check each allowed static door.
//devDependencies: @olai/log is here for its `./testlib` DECODER only: the readiness signal this suite waits on is a line on the server's stdout, and that line's format belongs to @olai/log — so the thing that reads it back is @olai/log's too, rather than a regex this suite would maintain alone and silently stop matching the day a value needed quoting. playwright is pinned to 1.61.1 — the version of `pkgs.playwright-driver` in this tree's overlay. The npm package ships only the driver's JS; the browsers come from the Nix store via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, and the driver refuses a browser build it was not compiled against. A minor-version drift here (kolu's 1.59.0, say) does not fail at install time — it fails at `chromium.launch()` with "Executable doesn't exist", pointing at a path inside the store that is real but wrong. Bump this only together with the overlay, never on its own.
